title: A Ghost for the Extraction
premise: Gideon Yarrow, a sleepless interpreter for a doomed peace delegation, is the only living witness to Flight 4471—a transport carrying negotiators that was erased from every radar, manifest, and memory bank while still airborne. Hunted by the extraction network that trained them and betrayed by the handlers they once trusted, Gideon must decide whether loyalty to the people who made them matters more than the truth of what happened in the sky. As the network closes in, Gideon uncovers that their own missing memories hold the flight's final minutes. In the end, Gideon burns the training program from within, choosing truth over the only family they've ever known—and finally sleeps.
about_author: Rosalind Whitlock is a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade in conflict zones before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose words are the most dangerous things they carry.

chapters.title: The Insomniac's Ear
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Interpreting at a fractious peace summit in Vellmar, Gideon mishears a delegate's phrase—a slip their training should make impossible. That night, unable to sleep, they notice a colleague's name has vanished from the delegation roster. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Boarding the delegation's transport home, Gideon experiences a violent déjà vu: the seat numbers, the pilot's voice, all familiar from a dream. Mid-flight, the cabin lights die for eleven seconds. When they land, ground control has no record the plane ever took off. Beat: reality tilts.

chapters.title: Eleven Seconds
chapters.summary: Alternate POV: Mara Osei, delegation security chief, reviewing airport footage that shows an empty runway where the plane landed. She confronts Gideon privately; both realize they remember different versions of the flight. Beat: uneasy alliance formed in shared gaslighting.

chapters.title: The Handler's Smile
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Their old handler, Casimir Brandt, appears uninvited at Gideon's hotel—warm, paternal, wrong. He offers Gideon a quiet reassignment and a pill 'for the dreams.' Gideon pockets the pill instead of taking it. Beat: loyalty begins to curdle into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Roster Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara pulls personnel files and finds Gideon's service record ends seven years earlier—with a death notice. She shows Gideon their own obituary. Beat: identity fracture; Gideon realizes parts of their past are manufactured.

chapters.title: The School Beneath the Lake
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, flashback-tinged. Following a buried memory, Gideon travels to a decommissioned lakeside facility where interpreters were trained—and where something else was taught after hours. A caretaker recognizes them and flees. Beat: grief for a self they can't retrieve.

chapters.title: Interference Pattern
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara decodes radio logs from the night of Flight 4471 and finds a repeating phrase in an obscure dialect—the same phrase Gideon 'misheard' at the summit. It's not gibberish; it's a kill-code. Beat: the conspiracy acquires a shape.

chapters.title: Burning the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Assassins hit Gideon's safehouse; Mara extracts them through flooding tunnels beneath the city. In the escape, Gideon instinctively uses a hand signal only the network teaches—revealing they were more than an interpreter. Beat: trust tested by revelation.

chapters.title: Casimir's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cornered by Mara, Casimir admits Flight 4471 carried delegates who'd discovered the network's true product: programmable memory. The erasure wasn't a crash cover-up—it was a demonstration. Beat: horror reframed as commerce.

chapters.title: The Passenger List That Isn't
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon finds a hidden passenger manifest in their own childhood keepsakes—placed there by someone who knew they'd come looking. Their mother's name is on it. Beat: personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: Sleep, When It Comes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, quiet chapter. Drugged-free for the first time in years, Gideon finally sleeps and dreams the flight's last eleven seconds in full: a voice reading the kill-code in their own handwriting. Beat: tenderness and terror intertwined.

chapters.title: Traitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara discovers Casimir fed her the decoded logs deliberately—he's playing both sides to protect a daughter enrolled in the program. She must choose between arresting him and using him. Beat: loyalty vs. truth, mirrored.

chapters.title: The Summit That Never Was
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The peace delegation reconvenes under new management; Gideon realizes the entire negotiation is staged theater to showcase the memory technology to buyers. They are the demo. Beat: claustrophobic escalation.

chapters.title: Hand Signals in the Dark
chapters.summary: Gideon and Mara POV alternating. Working covertly inside the summit, the two communicate through interpreter's gestures alone, planning sabotage while interpreting live. Beat: intimacy forged under surveillance.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon breaches the network's archive and finds recordings of their own erased sessions—including the moment their memories of Flight 4471 were taken. They hear themselves beg. Beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: Casimir's Confession, Part Two
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Casimir reveals he placed the manifest among Gideon's keepsakes—he's been grooming Gideon as the network's destroyer since the beginning, believing only a trained ghost can burn it down. Beat: betrayal and blessing in one breath.

chapters.title: Countdown at the Auction
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The network hosts its buyer demonstration: live memory-wipe of a volunteer delegate. Mara triggers the building lockdown as Gideon moves for the master archive. Beat: ticking clock, no exits.

chapters.title: The Kill-Code Spoken Backwards
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax part one. Confronting the network's director, Gideon recites the kill-code inverted—not to erase, but to restore, broadcasting every stolen memory to every attendee simultaneously. Beat: weaponized truth.

chapters.title: Fire Takes the Building
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The archive burns; Casimir dies holding the door so the restored witnesses escape, his daughter among them. Gideon carries out the last drive and lets the rest melt. Beat: sacrifice transfiguring loyalty.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Before an inquiry that wants tidy lies, Gideon testifies to the whole ugly truth, knowing it will cost them protection, career, and anonymity. Mara corroborates. Beat: truth chosen over safety, at price.

chapters.title: The Quiet Country
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon visits the lake facility one last time, now a school again, children learning languages for honest reasons. They leave flowers on a bench where their mother's name is carved. Beat: mourning turned gentle.

chapters.title: First Morning
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, coda. Months later, Gideon wakes without an alarm, having slept through the night for the first time since the incident. Mara brings coffee; the world is ordinary. Beat: resolution—memory kept, duty released, love allowed.
